lines: Russia ruled Warsaw, and its university barred women.
So she and her sister studied at a secret Floating University,
then worked for years as a governess.
In 1891, she finally reached Paris.
In eighteen ninety-one, she finally reached Paris.

lines: She married the physicist Pierre Curie.
In 1898, they found two new elements:
In eighteen ninety-eight, they found two new elements:
polonium, named for Poland, and radium.
In a leaky old shed,
they processed a ton of ore for over three years
to extract a tenth of a gram of radium.
In 1903, she shared the Nobel Prize in Physics,
In nineteen oh three, she shared the Nobel Prize in Physics,

Three years later, Pierre died in a street accident.
She took his post: the first woman to teach at the Sorbonne.
In 1911, she won a second Nobel, in Chemistry.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 4  X-ray cars at the front
lines: When World War One began, she realised
X-rays could help doctors find bullets in wounded soldiers.
She built mobile X-ray cars, learned to drive,
and took her daughter Irène, seventeen, to the front.
They also set up two hundred X-ray rooms in hospitals.
